components: Literary Theory 1: Key Concepts and Traditions
Restricted choice set by the programme: non-native speakers of English take Pronunciation (L_ETBAALG002, 3 EC); native speakers take Presentation (L_ETBAALG009, 3 EC).
Creative Writing and the Publishing Industry
Novel and Identity: Women Writers in the Eighteenth Century
Bachelor Thesis Literature and Society English

core: Close reading, genre and literary analysis across textual forms
Literary theory: multiple critical perspectives (humanist, feminist, Marxist, psychoanalytic) applied to interpretation
Literature's relationship to society, culture and everyday social life
Text-image and text-screen relationships: adaptation, film and visual culture
World and historical literary traditions from ancient texts to contemporary forms
The English-track literary-critical specialisation "Literature in a Changing World"
Creative writing practice across life narrative, poetry and performance; depth differs by track
Scriptwriting, podcasting and intermedial/adapted storytelling across media
Authorial style and voice, with dedicated practice differing by track
Literary-historical grounding for creative practice, from the Middle Ages to the present
adjacent: Language, style and linguistic choice in meaning-making
Publishing, editing and the professional literary/cultural field
questions: How does literature and storytelling respond to and shape contemporary social challenges?
What makes a story or text powerful, and how do creative and rhetorical choices in form and language shape its effect on an audience?
How is meaning produced across text, image and adapted media, and how do adaptations reshape stories for new audiences and forms?

Companion contribution: extends the programme's text-image and cultural-historical concerns to the modern visual arts and their institutions

Research-based analysis of race in American media and podcast assessment; partially addresses storytelling and power without substituting African/Caribbean literary study.
Companion philosophy of emotion includes aesthetic responses to fiction; it does not teach literary composition or authorial voice.

Actual training in rhetorical argumentation, essay structure and oral presentation. Text production overlap is partial; translation/editing and literary publishing are absent.

Practice-based public speaking, debate and storytelling taught through community-engaged work with children. This is oral rhetorical pedagogy, not scriptwriting, poetry composition or a guaranteed future named partner.
Actual close reading and creative work in poetry, voice, sound and performance, then hybrid projects; does not promise songwriting, fiction sequence or film-script production.
Actual literary survey from Gilgamesh to post-modernity, with primary and critical readings across genres; broad literary substance, not dedicated British/American historical sequences.
Study and production of structured personal narratives with life-writing theory; genuine literary analysis and bounded creative nonfiction practice.
Analysis of American mainstream and platform media, representation and storytelling; not a production course in scripts, podcasts or TikTok creation.

alternatives.label: Literary studies, theory and cultural interpretation
alternatives.concept: Close reading, literary theory, a broad literary survey, world myth, life writing, stylistics and film adaptation form the literary core. Creative poetry and performance add practice, while media, art history, sociology and philosophy offer different tools for interpreting culture. Specialist English literary periods, postcolonial sequences, publishing and compulsory thesis remain different from VU.
alternatives.labelReason: Names the actual literary study and the distinct interpretive or creative/public-rhetorical emphasis, without claiming complete specialist or Dutch-track equivalence.
progression: Actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings checked for every placement; firstyear PPD; introductory literary and rhetorical study precedes later analysis/practice. All24unique/180EC/fourperterm/atleast6advanced. No formal workbook prerequisite invented.

alternatives.label: Literature, creative practice and public rhetoric
alternatives.concept: Literary interpretation and theory support life-narrative writing, experimental poetry and performance, public rhetoric and a short documentary project. This direction gives more space to producing and presenting texts and media. It does not supply a Dutch-language creative-writing degree, sustained fiction or scriptwriting workshops, publishing training or a compulsory thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Names the actual literary study and the distinct interpretive or creative/public-rhetorical emphasis, without claiming complete specialist or Dutch-track equivalence.
progression: Actual workbook prerequisites and assigned-term offerings checked for every placement; firstyear PPD; introductory literary and rhetorical study precedes later analysis/practice. All24unique/180EC/fourperterm/atleast6advanced. No formal workbook prerequisite invented.
alternatives.distinctness: 5 courses (37.5 EC) differ each way. The primary uses intercultural/mind philosophy, media archaeology, environmental media analysis, Renaissance and museum interpretation; the related direction instead uses philosophy of emotion, modern sociology, contemporary media, oral community rhetoric and documentary production. Literary theory is retained in both. These are actual changes in disciplinary objects and production practice, not claims that companion social science supplies creative-writing craft.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no specific route. "Literature and Society: English" shares the parent programme's own name and its academic core is literary-critical analysis and literature-and-society content, directly continuing the generic programme's stated identity, while "Creatief Schrijven Nederlands" is explicitly marketed as a distinct, more specialised creative-writing professional track.

selection.assessment: Retain two qualified alternatives after substantive correction. Primary now contains all six actual literary courses45EC plus literary stylistics7.5, creative poetry/performance7.5 and rhetoric7.5:67.5EC of actual literary/textual/writing study; media30EC and art history30EC provide adjacent interpretive context, not missing literary periods or specialist research. Replace archaeology/socialpsychology with actual literarysurvey/lifenarrative, and replace broad persuasion with creative laboratory through a feasible term rearrangement; primaryno longer rests on only fourliteraturecourses30EC. Second has sixliterarycourses45EC plus stylistics,creative laboratory,rhetoric and community rhetoric30EC=75EC textual/communication contribution, plus film/media/documentary30EC. Added advanced literary theory and research-podcast media study replace socialpsychology and philosophyofself, which does not teach authorialvoice. Only15EC is direct sustained life-narrative/creative laboratory production; oralcommunityrhetoric, media analysis and shortdocumentary practice are distinct contributions, not fiction/scriptwritingworkshop sequences or Dutchlanguage training. The primary emphasises literarytheory/culturalinterpretation; second production,life-writing,oralrhetoric and documentary practice. Five exclusive courses37.5ECeachway establish actual distinctness. Retained coreclose reading, theory,multipletextualgenres,stylistics andadaptation supports a qualified response to Englishliteratureandsociety, with creative-related direction. Neither reproduces systematic British/American/earlymodern/eighteenthcentury/postcolonialliterature sequences, globalsociolinguistics, translation/editing/publishing, Dutchliteraryhistory/creativewriting sequence, or compulsoryindividualthesis. General sociology/psychology/philosophy are companions, not literarymethods or voicecraft. Shared filmadaptation supports visualcultureinterest partly but not entire specialistpath; ChangingWorldAfrican/Caribbeantexts remainsgap. Thirdcandidate lacks evidence-backed distinct disciplinarysequence; numericalcourse reshuffling is insufficient. No blanket claim that everygeneratorinterest is fully covered.

blocks: Partial curricular relationship. Both introduce close reading and the analysis of literary form across poetry, fiction and drama, with the critical terminology of literary analysis; VU frames the course around English literature.

Partial curricular relationship. Both teach principal traditions of literary theory, including Marxist and feminist criticism, and apply them to interpreting texts; VU also covers New Criticism and postcolonial theory, while UCR also covers humanist, cultural-minority and psychoanalytic perspectives.

Partial overlap in selfhood across Western and Buddhist thought. VU teaches intercultural philosophical method and critiques Eurocentric reason across cultures; UCR primarily studies mind, consciousness and personal identity.

Partial curricular relationship. Both analyse how cultural texts expose injustice, support resistance and emancipation, and imagine better futures; VU studies literary texts across several centuries, whereas UCR studies film, photography, music and podcasts in relation to race in American history.

The selected UCR programmes do not include a course on contemporary literature and globalization. Modern History covers political and economic history since 1815 without literary texts, and World Myth & Literature compares ancient myth across cultures rather than literature in a globalized world.

Partial curricular relationship. Both analyse how literary and dramatic texts are adapted to film and what adaptation changes; VU focuses on Shakespeare's plays, while UCR covers literature-to-film adaptation generally.

Partial curricular relationship. Both train ecocritical analysis of how texts and images represent relations between humans, nonhuman others and the environment; VU applies this to early modern literature (1550-1700), while UCR applies it to modern visual and audiovisual media.
Partial curricular relationship. Both study life-writing genres (autobiography, memoir, diary, travel narrative and blog) and their theory, and both include students' own writing of life narratives.

Partial curricular relationship. Both combine close reading of writers' formal techniques with a workshop in which students draft, receive feedback on and revise their own creative work; UCR's course centres on poetry, performance and experimental forms.

Partial curricular relationship. Both analyse how linguistic choices at sentence and discourse level, such as stance, modality and cohesion, shape meaning; VU applies this to students' own academic English writing and editing, whereas UCR's stylistics course analyses mainly literary texts.

Partial curricular relationship. Both train students to shape their own texts for specific audiences and purposes by adapting structure, style and register; UCR approaches this through classical and modern rhetoric and does not cover the translation and editing parts of the VU course.
The selected UCR programmes do not include a course on the publishing industry; UCR offers no dedicated publishing or editorial-production course.

Partial curricular relationship. Both study how cultural objects are made, valued, preserved and passed on, with art history as a shared discipline; VU spans antiquity to the present across several disciplines, while UCR focuses on Western painting from the late Middle Ages onward and its institutions.
Literary history, specialisation and English studies
No dedicated modern American literary-history course. Great Literary Works adds a broad historical literary survey; Media & Race and Histories of Gender study other cultural/historical objects.
The selected UCR programmes do not include a course dedicated to British literary history; related broad literary-survey content, where present, is distributed elsewhere.

The selected UCR programmes do not include a course on transatlantic or nineteenth-century travel writing. Life & Travel Writing covers travel narrative but is aligned with Life Writing, where its overlap is stronger.

The selected UCR programmes do not include a course on the eighteenth-century novel or women's writing. Histories of Gender studies gender in nineteenth- to twenty-first-century American history, not literary analysis of the novel.
The selected UCR programmes do not include a sociolinguistics or global-English course; UCR offers no equivalent study of English as a global language.

The selected UCR programmes do not include a course on African or postcolonial literature. Media & Race studies race and power in American media, not short stories and comics from the African continent and diaspora.
The selected UCR programmes do not include a course on Caribbean or postcolonial literature, and no equivalent of the student-organised research symposium that forms this module's main assessment.
Academic skills, language, formation and elective space

Partial curricular relationship. Both teach core academic skills: defining a research focus, finding and using academic sources, and structuring an argued essay; VU's module is a literary-studies research-writing module using MLA citation, while UCR's course also covers personal, ethical and civic development.

No separate scheduled counterpart for this continuation of literary research writing. PPD supplies general academic formation; qualitative social research is not literary source/close-reading methodology.
This is a compulsory academic-English language module; UCR's English-medium curriculum has no equivalent standalone component.
This is a compulsory academic-English language module; UCR's English-medium curriculum has no equivalent standalone component.

This is a 3-EC English-language unit whose option depends on native-speaker status. UCR has no English pronunciation training. The Art of Rhetorical Communication overlaps with the Presentation option's oral-delivery skills but is aligned with Text Production, Translation, and Editing, and it does not address the Pronunciation option.

This is a compulsory career-orientation module graded complete/incomplete (strengths, professional profiles, networking, CVs and interviews); no scheduled UCR course is dedicated to career preparation, and Personal & Professional Development is aligned with Academic Skills 1.
This is the comparator's independent-research component. UCR's standardized Optional independent research element is displayed against it rather than a specific scheduled course.

This is open elective/minor space that VU students fill freely from a catalogue of minors, a free choice of units, or an internship; it is preserved generically rather than matched to an invented UCR course.

notes.text: These alternatives retain genuine literary analysis, theory, a broad literary survey, world myth, life writing, stylistics and adaptation. VU additionally provides systematic English literary periods and postcolonial specialisation, global-English linguistics, translation, publishing, language training and a compulsory 12 EC individual thesis. The UCR programmes have a different distribution of disciplinary study; optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.

The related direction combines bounded life-writing and experimental poetry practice with rhetoric, literary analysis and documentary work. Media analysis is not scriptwriting instruction, and community rhetoric is oral pedagogy. It does not reproduce the Dutch-track literary history, language, three-year creative-writing sequence, publishing or final creative research work.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Literature and Society studies how literary texts shape and respond to culture and society. The English track combines close reading and theory with English literary history, language, creative writing and publishing, followed by a specialisation and individual thesis. A separate Dutch track concentrates on creative writing and Dutch literature.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two qualified UCR alternatives develop literary study through cultural interpretation or through creative practice and public rhetoric. Both contain substantial actual literary work. Their companion media and social-science courses offer different perspectives, with less specialist English literary depth and no complete Dutch creative-writing or publishing sequence.

curriculum.routeLabel: Literature and Society: English; Literature in a Changing World
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC illustration includes one 3 EC Pronunciation or Presentation option, one 12 EC specialisation pair, an individual 12 EC thesis and 30 EC of approved open study. Language testing or a refresher, academic orientation, attendance and course-entry conditions apply. All first- and second-year courses must be passed before the spring thesis. The open space is not a fixed minor or compulsory exchange. Future offerings may change.
